t:
Section 301 (a) of said Act, as amended, is further amended—

    (1) 
By striking out of paragraph (1) the words “under title II, or title VI” and inserting in lieu thereof the words “under title II, title VI, or title VIII”; and
 
    (2) 
By striking out the period and adding the following proviso at the end of paragraph (1) (E) :“: Provided, That such aggregate amount paid by the Association shall not include any amount paid by it for a mortgage or mortgages which are insured under title VIII of this Act; and”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that adds title VIII mortgages to a cross-reference and excludes them from an aggregate purchase limit for the Association. A tempting reading might treat the reference to the Association or to mortgages as involving outside parties, but nothing here calls for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Provided, That such aggregate amount paid by the Association shall not include any amount paid by it for a mortgage or mortgages which are insured under title VIII of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute, specifically modifying the text of Section 301(a) to include 'title VIII' in a list of titles. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative drafting language.
qwen_block.s: By striking out of paragraph (1) the words “under title II, or title VI” and inserting in lieu thereof the words “under title II, title VI, or title VIII”; and

opus.w: This section only makes technical changes to cross-references and dollar limits on the Association's mortgage purchases under the National Housing Act. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The mention of the Association and insured mortgages describes financial transactions, not outside participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: Provided, That such aggregate amount paid by the Association shall not include any amount paid by it for a mortgage or mortgages which are insured under title VIII of this Act
opus.b:
I'd label this **No**.

1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The text mentions "the Association" (the Federal National Mortgage Association) and insured mortgages. That might suggest outside companies or the public are involved. They aren't. This is a technical amendment that adds title VIII mortgages to the Association's purchase authority and leaves them out of an aggregate dollar limit. No outside party is consulted about any federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute regarding the calculation of aggregate amounts paid by an Association for insurance purposes. It does not create any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or other forms of participation as defined. The text merely clarifies financial definitions and exclusions.
qwen_chat.s: By striking out the period and adding the following proviso at the end of paragraph (1) (E) :“: Provided, That such aggregate amount paid by the Association shall not include any amount paid by it for a mortgage or mortgages which are insured under title VIII of this Act; and”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends a statute involving an "Association" (likely the Federal Home Loan Bank Association), it implies some form of interaction or participation. However, the text itself is purely technical, dealing with the definition of what counts towards an aggregate payment limit for insurance purposes. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties.
